data/proposals/retire-carried-findings-satisfied-by-downstream-work.md says "That job's own reviewer recorded both as handled (`data/reviews/j-20260904-04.md:31-33` and `:186-188`)". Both of those ranges are about the FrontierMath finding only — :31-33 reads "it prints the release page's table figure of 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2) directly beside the same page's prose claim", and :186-188 reads "The post prints both and says which is which". The reviewer's confirmation of the first finding (the closing sentence quoted in full) is at :263-266: "The quotation of this site's own earlier post ... is verbatim the last sentence of `content/blog/openai-astra-critical-designation.md:57`." Replacing ":31-33" with ":263-266" would make the citation say what the record says. Nothing downstream depends on it — both findings are verifiable in the post itself — but the proposal's argument is built on cited line ranges and one of them points at the wrong finding.

items.detail:
verify-daybreak-defense-network-product-wording.md says "a plain `user-agent`-only fetch returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare challenge); the successful request sent `accept-language: en-US,en;q=0.9` and `cache-control: no-cache` alongside a full Chrome UA." That did not reproduce on 2026-09-04 from this machine: a fetch sending ONLY the same full Chrome `user-agent` returned HTTP 200 with 375,911 bytes, while a fetch sending no headers at all (Node's default UA) returned HTTP 403 with 9,861 bytes. So the header that clears the challenge is the UA alone; `accept-language` and `cache-control` were not load-bearing. The fix is to restate the note as "a fetch with no browser user-agent returns 403; sending a full Chrome UA returns 200", or to drop the causal claim and record only the headers that were sent. Nothing else in the file depends on this — the retrieval it describes reproduces exactly. Note that Cloudflare gating is IP- and time-dependent, so the author may well have observed the 403 they recorded; the note is unreliable as a general instrument claim rather than dishonest.

items.detail:
The evidence file's header says the raw transcript is a "node fetch+strip+count script, 2026-09-03; the huggingface.co/meta-models org page was fetched twice because its activity feed renders intermittently". Grepping "^=== https" over data/reviews/evidence/verify-meta-spark-weights-pending-status.raw.txt returns 11 fetch blocks and huggingface.co/meta-models appears exactly once (line 22). The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.
